Header: Acanthoplus spp. e.g. A. speiseri Armoured ground cricket, Armoured bush cricket

Prevention: October at the beginning of rainy season.
Plant short duration varieties, such as
Kuyuma, or short- medium duration varieties such as
NS551 (red var.) (early harvesting also prevents bird damage).
Or at least mix short duration varieties with long duration varieties such as
Note that long duration varieties may suffer from drought.
Clean up weeds in and around field weekly (once per season is not enough)
Dig ½ m deep and ½ m wide trenches around field to prevent crickets walking/ jumping into field (crickets are wingless).
Mix sorghum with cowpea, mung bean or melons to prevent damage in current season.
This may increase egg laying and damage in next season.
Monitoring: Survey for presence of the crickets, they may sit on bushes.
Visit field and nearby sites 1x per week particularly in the dry season:
Note, that cricket eggs will hatch after the first heavy rains, and crickets may then damage the upcoming sorghum
You may consider applying direct control measures when about 10 to 50 crickets are found per 1m3 bush, or 1 to 5 per m2 ground, or 1 per sorghum plant on average.
Direct Control: Spray neem-based solutions (50 w %), on areas with young crickets every two weeks.
Ask your local agro-input suppliers to organise such products if neem trees do not grow in your area.
Tephrosia leaf solution (20 w%) every 2 weeks
Daily handpick crickets from nearby bushes or from infested crop, then crush or kill them in plastic bags (suffocation or sun heat) and then feed them to poultry.
All this may be conducted at same time when scaring
Quelea birds that also damage sorghum.
Do not leave crushed crickets in field as they attract new crickets.
Restrictions: Spray insecticides on tall shady non-food and non-flowering vegetation where there are many crickets e.g. onto nearby bushes.
Or spray only on heavily infested parts of the field.
There is often no need to spray the entire field.
Apply on a calm day during morning or evening

When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre- harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.

Spray a 2.5m wide strip of fipronil – based products around the field or into the trenches as a barrier.
Spay max twice with min 7 day interval.
Mix bran (attracts crickets) with small amount of carbaryl and add small portions into trenches around field.
